target_customer: Indian college graduates and freshers who pay for tech skilling and placement, plus hiring partner companies that recruit them
problem: Fresh graduates in India struggle to get tech jobs, and campus hiring was done mostly by hand and reached few colleges.
business_model: Paid courses for students with placement support, plus free hiring drives for partner companies (originally a per student hired fee from companies)
product_category: Edtech, tech skilling and campus placement

founders.name: Yashwardhan Burad
founders.background_notes: Described as IIT Delhi graduate on the company site. Listed as co-founder by Inc42 (2020).

founders.name: Harsh Sharma
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and CTO per company site.

founders.name: Priyanshu Agarwal
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and COO per company site.

founders.name: Vishu Bansal
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and CPO per company site; YC page says he leads partnerships.

technical_complexity.rationale: A placement SaaS for colleges and an online training product were standard web engineering. The hard part was operations and hiring partner relationships, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Course content and campus drives were easy to copy. Relationships with colleges and hiring partners gave limited lock in. Inc42 (2020) reported few colleges used the original SaaS effectively.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied the model. The company pivoted to training and later opened offline centres (Noida, March 2024).

market_need_then: Indian campus hiring was reported by the CEO (YourStory, May 2019) as mostly manual, and Inc42 (June 2020) reported on campus drive conversion of only 4 to 5 percent, showing candidates lacked job readiness.

identity.visual_style: Not described by any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Placement outcome claims such as 2000+ placed and 500+ hiring partners, taglines about launching a tech career

brand_strength.rationale: Sources show only the company's own taglines and badges (Backed by Y Combinator, LinkedIn Top Companies listing). No press on the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Placement SaaS for colleges, charging companies per student hired
pivots.to: Soft skills and technical training for students
pivots.why: Few colleges used the SaaS well and campus drive conversion was 4 to 5 percent (Inc42, 2020)

pivots.to: Offline first skill centres, first in Noida
pivots.why: Stated on YC page, reason not given

outcome_analysis: AccioJob is still active with about 120 people. It raised small rounds (a Rs 1.25 crore seed in 2019 and a Mynavi investment in 2023) and survived by pivoting from placement SaaS to training, then to online courses in 2020 and offline skill centres from 2024. It claims 2,000 plus students placed. It is a modest capital efficient business rather than a venture scale outlier so far, and the claims are the company's own.
notes: The 2019 round of Rs 1.25 crore (YourStory and People Matters, search snippets; YourStory page returned 403) was left without a USD amount because no source gave one. Inc42 (June 2020) reported total funding of $165.66K with Hershel Mehta (Mehta Ventures) and Sanjay Mehta (100X.VC) as backers. The 2023 amount is undisclosed by People Matters; CB Insights about $2.71M is an aggregator figure, unverified. Competitors named by Inc42 in June 2020 (Naukri, LinkedIn, Shine, Internshala, HireMee, stuMagz, Twenty19, Letsintern, Superset) are about 15 months after the batch, so they are not listed in competition_at_founding. No dated source near the 2019 batch was found. No outcome news found (no layoffs, acquisition or shutdown). Founder prior employers not found in opened sources. Name origin not stated by any opened source.
